gen-dafont-early-gameboy-instrument-sans: Early GameBoy stretches its letters wide with a skyward x-height and a mild thick-thin lilt, while Instrument Sans keeps every stroke uniform. Playful on top, tidy below.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-space-grotesk: Commanding but playful, Early GameBoy towers with its tall lowercase and lightly swollen curves. Space Grotesk sits lower beneath it, drawing each glyph as one ribbon of constant width, so the two feel like loud and quiet voices sharing a line.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-alpino: Cast-iron stature, no wobble. Edo SZ gives every stroke the same gauge, and Alpino's tall body makes its ascenders look short; shrink the heading and that gap would tighten.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Edo SZ gives its lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals, each stroke held to a single width. And Be Vietnam Pro follows with curve endings that never crowd, its bent-steel strokes and high mean line making a lighter counterweight.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-bespoke-sans: Sharp and refined, Bespoke Sans leaves generous space between its curve ends and the stem. And Edo SZ, with letterforms like bent tubing, gives that openness a sturdy, low-slung partner to lean against.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-fira-sans: Cast iron, but friendly. Edo SZ stands on tall lowercase with one constant stroke, and Fira Sans answers with s curves flung wide at both ends and no thick-thin contrast, a generous x-height keeping the text easy.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-savate: Edo SZ never tapers, every stroke cut as if no quill ever pressed. Savate reads smoothly over a long stretch, its heavy stems easing into lighter curves and its tall rounded o nearly matching a capital.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-montserrat: Cultural and classic, Edo SZ stands up with a lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals. And Montserrat slips in beneath, its oversized e and a counters leaving plenty of white space for the eye to glide through.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-satoshi: Edo SZ carries the stature of cast iron capitals in lowercase, every stroke held to one constant width. Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height and an open e, so a long read stays easy.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-sora: Edo SZ stands tall, its lowercase built like cast iron capitals. Sora sits lower in height, with no pressure swell at the curves and a c and s kept widely parted, so the heading dominates while the text stays precise.
